By any historical definition, the United States today is a tyranny.

What an interesting article. I felt the opposite. Although I agree with his conclusion, the way he argues for it was just annoying. He should have just came out and said what he believed the United States to be rather than trying to define it and debate its existence in the same way.

It reminds me of those philosophy classes where people debate whether or not perfect circles really exist, or those classes where Kantian philosophers intellectually masturbate over train-driven ethically justified homicide allegories.

I found myself wondering when he would get to the damn point and stop defining every word like a middle school speech writer.

I disagree. As a mathematician I appreciate how clearly everything was defined. Often when people debate they use ambiguous terms to mean how they view them without regard to the words' literal meanings. I find this less constructive because it is difficult to reach a common ground when people disagree what the words mean. The problem is exacerbated when people don't notice that they are using words differently and this can cause tensions to run high due to misunderstandings. I can see how the article seemed tedious but ultimately it felt precise not arduous to me. The author spoke directly and non-euphemistically which I admired.
It was very precise, and I found myself agreeing with the way he defined his terms. My assessment probably says more about me than it does about the author.
